units.en: Dezong ascended the throne in Dali 14 and changed the era name to Jianzhong the following year. At that time the shortened-month mourning regulation was in force, so he performed the ceremony in cap and robe.
units.literal: Dezong ascended the throne in the fourteenth year of Dali; the next year he changed the era name to Jianzhong; at the time the shortened-month regulation was in force; therefore he performed the affair in cap and robe.

units.zh: 今陛下退朝之服，盡如禮製，謂當供張別殿，遣三公奉冊，冊藏於有司，恭俟來歸。
units.en: Now Your Majesty's dress after retiring from court fully follows ritual regulation. I propose that a separate hall be prepared, the Three Ducal Ministers be dispatched to present the patent, the patent be stored with the relevant offices, and the ceremony await her return with all due respect.
units.literal: Now Your Majesty's dress after retiring from court fully follows ritual regulation; I say that a separate hall should be set out, the Three Ducal Ministers dispatched to present the patent, the patent stored with the relevant offices, and respectfully awaited until her return.

units.zh: 願下禮官講明。”
units.en: I ask that the ritual officers be ordered to clarify this matter."
units.literal: I wish that ritual officers below be ordered to clarify this."

units.zh: 詔從之。
units.en: An edict approved the proposal.
units.literal: An edict followed this.

units.zh: 禮部、太常言：“寶文欲乞以‘ 皇太后寶’四字為文，合差撰冊文官一員，書冊文官一員，書篆寶文官一員，並差執政。”
units.en: The Ministry of Rites and the Temple of Rites reported: "For the seal inscription we request the four characters 'Empress Dowager's Seal.' One official should be assigned to draft the patent text, one to inscribe it, and one to inscribe the seal text in seal script; all should be drawn from the chief ministers."
units.literal: The Ministry of Rites and the Temple of Rites said: "For the seal inscription we wish to request using the four characters 'Empress Dowager's Seal' as the text; in all one official should be assigned to draft the patent text, one to inscribe the patent text, and one to inscribe the seal text in seal script; all should be drawn from the chief ministers."

units.zh: 十年，營建皇太后宮，以慈寧為名。
units.en: In the tenth year, the empress dowager's palace was built and named Cining.
units.literal: In the tenth year, the empress dowager's palace was constructed, taking Cining as its name.

units.zh: 十二月，帝自常禦殿詣慈寧殿遙賀皇 太后，奉上冊寶。
units.en: In the twelfth month the emperor proceeded from Changyu Hall to Cining Hall to offer congratulations from afar to the empress dowager and present the patent and seal.
units.literal: In the twelfth month, the emperor, from Changyu Hall, proceeded to Cining Hall to offer congratulations from afar to the empress dowager and present the patent and seal.

units.zh: 十二年八月，皇太后還慈寧宮，十月十八日，奉進冊寶。
units.en: In the eighth month of the twelfth year the empress dowager returned to Cining Palace. On the eighteenth day of the tenth month the patent and seal were formally presented.
units.literal: In the eighth month of the twelfth year, the empress dowager returned to Cining Palace; on the eighteenth day of the tenth month, the patent and seal were presented.

units.zh: 其日張設慈寧殿，設坐殿中，皇太后服禕衣即御坐，本殿官設冊寶於殿下， 慈寧宮事務官並本殿官並朝服詣殿下，再拜，搢笏，舉冊寶奉進；
units.en: On that day Cining Hall was prepared and a seat placed in the hall. The empress dowager, wearing the yi robe, took the imperial seat. Officials of the hall set the patent and seal below the hall. Officials in charge of Cining Palace affairs and hall officials alike, in court dress, proceeded below the hall, bowed twice, inserted their tablets, and raised the patent and seal to present them;
units.literal: On that day Cining Hall was set out; a seat was placed in the hall; the empress dowager, wearing the yi robe, immediately took the imperial seat; officials of the hall set the patent and seal below the hall; officials in charge of Cining Palace affairs and officials of the hall alike, in court dress, proceeded below the hall, bowed twice, inserted their tablets, raised the patent and seal and presented them;

units.zh: 先進冊，次進寶，進畢，降坐，易禕衣，服常服。
units.en: the patent was presented first and then the seal. When the presentation was complete, she left the seat, changed out of the yi robe, and put on ordinary dress.
units.literal: first the patent was presented, next the seal; when presentation was complete, she descended from the seat, changed out of the yi robe, and wore ordinary dress.

units.zh: 皇帝詣慈寧殿賀，如宮中儀，次宰臣率百僚拜表 稱賀。
units.en: The emperor proceeded to Cining Hall to offer congratulations according to inner-palace ceremony. Chief ministers then led all officials in bowing and submitting congratulatory memorials.
units.literal: The emperor proceeded to Cining Hall to offer congratulations, as in inner-palace ceremony; next chief ministers led the hundred officials in bowing and presenting memorials of congratulation.

units.zh: 三十二年六月，詔上太上皇帝、太上皇后尊號，集議以聞。
units.en: In the sixth month of the thirty-second year, an edict ordered honorific titles for the Supreme Emperor and Supreme Empress, and deliberations were assembled and reported.
units.literal: In the sixth month of the thirty-second year, an edict ordered that honorific titles be conferred on the Supreme Emperor and Supreme Empress; deliberations were assembled and reported.

units.zh: 左仆射陳康伯等言：“五帝之壽，惟堯最高，百王之聖，惟堯獨冠。
units.en: Left Vice Director Chen Kangbo and others said: "Among the Five Emperors, only Yao lived longest; among the hundred kings, only Yao stood supreme in sagely virtue.
units.literal: Left Vice Director Chen Kangbo and others said: "Among the Five Emperors in longevity, only Yao was highest; among the hundred kings in sageliness, only Yao stood alone at the crown.

units.zh: 今茲高世之舉， 視堯有光，恭請上太上皇帝尊號曰光堯壽聖太上皇帝，太上皇后尊號曰壽聖太上皇后。”
units.en: Now this exalted act surpassing the age shines when compared with Yao. We respectfully request conferring on the Supreme Emperor the honorific title Guangyao Shousheng Supreme Emperor and on the Supreme Empress the honorific title Shousheng Supreme Empress."
units.literal: Now this exalted act surpassing the age sheds light when compared with Yao; we respectfully request conferring on the Supreme Emperor the honorific title Guangyao Shousheng Supreme Emperor, and on the Supreme Empress the honorific title Shousheng Supreme Empress."

units.zh: 詔恭依，仍令禮部、太常討論禮儀以聞。
units.en: An edict respectfully approved the proposal and ordered the Ministry of Rites and the Temple of Rites to discuss the ceremonial regulations and report.
units.literal: An edict respectfully followed this, and still ordered the Ministry of Rites and the Temple of Rites to discuss ceremonial propriety and report.

units.zh: 左仆射陳康伯撰太上皇帝冊文，兼 禮儀使、參政汪澈書冊文並篆寶，知樞密院葉義問撰太上皇后冊文，同知樞密院事黃祖舜書冊文。
units.en: Left Vice Director Chen Kangbo drafted the Supreme Emperor's patent text. Concurrent Commissioner of Ceremonial Propriety and Vice Grand Councilor Wang Che inscribed the patent text and carved the seal in seal script. Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Ye Yiwen drafted the Supreme Empress's patent text, and Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Huang Zushun inscribed it.
units.literal: Left Vice Director Chen Kangbo drafted the Supreme Emperor's patent text; Concurrent Commissioner of Ceremonial Propriety and Vice Grand Councilor Wang Che inscribed the patent text and carved the seal in seal script; Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Ye Yiwen drafted the Supreme Empress's patent text; Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Huang Zushun inscribed the patent text.

units.zh: 八月十四日，奉上冊寶。
units.en: On the fourteenth day of the eighth month the patent and seal were presented.
units.literal: On the fourteenth day of the eighth month, the patent and seal were presented.

units.zh: 是日，陪位文武百僚、太傅以下行事官，並朝服入詣大慶殿下立班。
units.en: On that day civil and military officials attending in place and acting officials from the Grand Preceptor downward, all in court dress, entered and took their ranks below Daqing Hall.
units.literal: On that day, civil and military officials of the hundred ranks attending in place, and acting officials from the Grand Preceptor downward, all in court dress entered, proceeded below Daqing Hall, and stood in ranks.

units.zh: 皇帝自內服履袍入禦幄，服通天冠、絳紗袍出至大慶殿，詣冊寶褥位前再拜，在位官皆再拜訖，皇帝行發冊寶授太傅之禮如儀。
units.en: The emperor, wearing court robes within, entered the imperial curtain. Wearing the Tongtian cap and crimson gauze robe he came forth to Daqing Hall, proceeded to the patent and seal cushion, and bowed twice. After all officials in attendance had bowed twice, the emperor performed the rite of issuing the patent and seal and presenting them to the Grand Preceptor according to ceremony.
units.literal: The emperor, from within wearing court robes, entered the imperial curtain; wearing the Tongtian cap and crimson gauze robe he came forth to Daqing Hall, proceeded before the patent and seal cushion and bowed twice; when all officials in attendance had bowed twice, the emperor performed the rite of issuing the patent and seal and presenting them to the Grand Preceptor according to ceremony.

units.zh: 禮畢，皇帝還幄，服履袍還內，文武百僚退。
units.en: When the rites were complete, the emperor returned to the curtain, changed into court robes, and returned to the inner palace. Civil and military officials withdrew.
units.literal: When the rites were complete, the emperor returned to the curtain, changed into court robes, and returned within; civil and military officials of the hundred ranks withdrew.

units.zh: 儀仗鼓吹，
units.en: Guard of honor and ceremonial music,
units.literal: Guard of honor and ceremonial music,

units.zh: 〈（備而不作。）〉
units.en: (Prepared but not performed.)
units.literal: (Prepared but not performed.)

units.zh: 護衛冊寶，太傅以下行事官導從冊寶至德壽宮。
units.en: escorted the patent and seal as acting officials from the Grand Preceptor downward guided them to Deshou Palace.
units.literal: escorting the patent and seal, acting officials from the Grand Preceptor downward guided and followed the patent and seal to Deshou Palace.

units.zh: 皇帝自祥曦殿服履袍乘輦，至德壽宮大次降輦，陪位文武官入殿庭立班定，太傅以下行 事官從冊寶入殿，皇帝服通天冠、絳紗袍升殿，詣西向褥位立，太上皇帝自宮服履袍即坐，皇帝北向四拜起居訖，次太傅以下皆四拜起居。
units.en: The emperor, wearing court robes, rode the imperial carriage from Xiangxi Hall. At the great side hall of Deshou Palace he dismounted. Civil and military officials attending in place entered the hall court and took their fixed ranks. Acting officials from the Grand Preceptor downward followed the patent and seal into the hall. The emperor, wearing the Tongtian cap and crimson gauze robe, ascended the hall and stood at the western-facing cushion. The Supreme Emperor, wearing court robes within the palace, took his seat. The emperor, facing north, bowed four times in reporting on his health. The Grand Preceptor and those below then all bowed four times in reporting on health.
units.literal: The emperor, from Xiangxi Hall wearing court robes, rode the imperial carriage; arriving at the great side hall of Deshou Palace he descended from the carriage; civil and military officials attending in place entered the hall court and stood in fixed ranks; acting officials from the Grand Preceptor downward followed the patent and seal into the hall; the emperor, wearing the Tongtian cap and crimson gauze robe, ascended the hall, proceeded to the western-facing cushion and stood; the Supreme Emperor, from within the palace wearing court robes, immediately took his seat; the emperor, facing north, four times bowed in reporting on health; next the Grand Preceptor and below all four times bowed in reporting on health.

units.zh: 次行奉冊之 禮，中書令、參知政事史浩讀冊，攝侍中葉義問讀寶，讀訖，退復位。
units.en: Next came the rite of presenting the patent. Director of the Secretariat and Vice Grand Councilor Shi Hao read the patent, and Acting Palace Attendant Ye Yiwen read the seal. When the reading was finished, they withdrew and returned to their places.
units.literal: Next the rite of presenting the patent was performed; Director of the Secretariat and Vice Grand Councilor Shi Hao read the patent; Acting Palace Attendant Ye Yiwen read the seal; when reading was finished, they withdrew and returned to their places.

units.zh: 皇帝再拜稱賀曰：“皇帝臣某稽首言：伏惟光堯壽聖太上皇帝陛下冊寶告成，鴻名肇正，與天 同壽，率土均歡。”
units.en: The emperor bowed twice and offered congratulations, saying: "The emperor, your subject, kowtows and reports: Humbly considering that Your Majesty the Guangyao Shousheng Supreme Emperor's patent and seal are now complete and the great name newly established, may you share Heaven's longevity; throughout the land all rejoice equally."
units.literal: The emperor bowed twice and offered congratulations, saying: "The emperor, your subject So-and-so, kowtows and says: Humbly considering that Your Majesty the Guangyao Shousheng Supreme Emperor's patent and seal are announced complete, the great name is newly established, sharing Heaven's longevity; throughout the land all equally rejoice."

units.zh: 皇帝再拜，次侍中承旨宣答曰：“皇帝孝通天地，禮備古今，勉受鴻名，良深感慰。”
units.en: The emperor bowed twice. The Palace Attendant then received instructions and proclaimed the reply: "The emperor's filial piety reaches through Heaven and Earth and his rites are complete through past and present. I reluctantly accept this great name, and my gratitude and consolation are profound."
units.literal: The emperor bowed twice; next the Palace Attendant received instructions and proclaimed the reply: "The emperor's filial piety penetrates Heaven and Earth; rites are complete through past and present; I reluctantly accept the great name, and my feeling of deep consolation is truly great."

units.zh: 皇帝再拜訖，西向立，次太傅以下再拜稱賀致詞曰：“攝 太傅、尚書左仆射臣康伯等稽首言：伏惟光堯壽聖太上皇帝陛下肅臨寶位，誕受丕稱，獨推天父之尊，普慰帝臣之願。”
units.en: When the emperor had finished bowing twice, he stood facing west. The Grand Preceptor and those below then bowed twice and offered congratulations with a formal address: "Acting Grand Preceptor and Director of the Left Secretariat, your subject Kangbo and others kowtow and report: Humbly considering that Your Majesty the Guangyao Shousheng Supreme Emperor solemnly presides over the throne and has newly received this great title, uniquely extending the honor due Heaven's father and universally fulfilling the wishes of the emperor's ministers."
units.literal: When the emperor had finished bowing twice, he stood facing west; next the Grand Preceptor and below bowed twice and offered congratulations with a formal address, saying: "Acting Grand Preceptor, Director of the Left Secretariat, your subject Kangbo and others kowtow and say: Humbly considering that Your Majesty the Guangyao Shousheng Supreme Emperor solemnly presides over the precious throne, newly receives the great title, uniquely extending the honor of Heaven's father, universally comforting the wishes of the emperor's ministers."

units.zh: 奏訖，再拜舞蹈。
units.en: When the address was finished, they bowed twice and performed the dance.
units.literal: When the memorial was finished, they bowed twice and performed the dance.

units.zh: 次侍中承旨宣答曰：“光 堯壽聖太上皇帝聖旨：倦勤滋久，佚老是圖，勉受嘉名，但增感慰。”
units.en: The Palace Attendant then received instructions and proclaimed the reply: "The Guangyao Shousheng Supreme Emperor's edict: Weariness in diligence has long grown; retirement and old age are my aim. I reluctantly accept this fine name, but my gratitude and consolation only increase."
units.literal: Next the Palace Attendant received instructions and proclaimed the reply: "The Guangyao Shousheng Supreme Emperor's holy edict: Weariness in diligence has long increased; retirement and old age are my aim; I reluctantly accept the fine name, but my feeling of gratitude and consolation only increases."

units.zh: 又再拜舞蹈。
units.en: Again they bowed twice and performed the dance.
units.literal: Again they bowed twice and performed the dance.

units.zh: 次太上皇帝降坐入宮，皇帝後從壽聖太上皇后冊寶入宮。
units.en: Next the Supreme Emperor left his seat and entered the palace. The emperor followed with the Shousheng Supreme Empress's patent and seal into the palace.
units.literal: Next the Supreme Emperor descended from the seat and entered the palace; the emperor followed afterward with the Shousheng Supreme Empress's patent and seal into the palace.

units.zh: 皇帝詣太 上皇后坐前北向立，太上皇后升坐，皇帝四拜起居，行奉上冊寶之禮，讀冊官陳子常讀冊，讀寶官梁康民讀寶，讀訖復位，皇帝再拜稱賀致詞曰：“皇帝臣某稽首 言：伏惟壽聖太上皇后殿下德茂坤元，禮崇大號，寶書翕受，歡抃無疆。”
units.en: The emperor proceeded before the Supreme Empress's seat and stood facing north. The Supreme Empress ascended and took her seat. The emperor bowed four times in reporting on her health and performed the rite of presenting the patent and seal. Patent Reader Chen Zichang read the patent and Seal Reader Liang Kangmin read the seal; when the reading was finished they returned to their places. The emperor bowed twice and offered congratulations with a formal address: "The emperor, your subject, kowtows and reports: Humbly considering that Your Highness the Shousheng Supreme Empress's virtue flourishes in the earth's origin and rites honor this great title, the precious document is graciously received and our joy knows no bounds."
units.literal: The emperor proceeded before the Supreme Empress's seat and stood facing north; the Supreme Empress ascended and took her seat; the emperor four times bowed in reporting on health; the rite of presenting the patent and seal was performed; Patent Reader Chen Zichang read the patent; Seal Reader Liang Kangmin read the seal; when reading was finished they returned to their places; the emperor bowed twice and offered congratulations with a formal address, saying: "The emperor, your subject So-and-so, kowtows and says: Humbly considering that Your Highness the Shousheng Supreme Empress's virtue flourishes in the earth's origin, rites honor the great title, the precious document is harmoniously received; joyful exultation is without bound."

units.zh: 皇帝再拜，次宣答官承旨宣答曰：“壽聖太上皇后教旨：皇帝祲容載蕆，顯號來膺，誠孝 通天，但深感惕。”
units.en: The emperor bowed twice. The reply-proclaiming official then received instructions and proclaimed the reply: "The Shousheng Supreme Empress's instruction: The emperor's reverent bearing carries deep sincerity; the illustrious title comes to be received; his sincere filial piety reaches through Heaven—but my feeling of deep reverence and caution is profound."
units.literal: The emperor bowed twice; next the reply-proclaiming official received instructions and proclaimed the reply: "The Shousheng Supreme Empress's instruction: The emperor's reverent bearing carries deep sincerity; the illustrious title comes to be received; sincere filial piety penetrates Heaven; but my feeling of deep reverence and caution is great."

units.zh: 皇帝再拜訖，太上皇后降坐入宮。
units.en: When the emperor had finished bowing twice, the Supreme Empress left her seat and entered the palace.
units.literal: When the emperor had finished bowing twice, the Supreme Empress descended from the seat and entered the palace.

units.zh: 次太傅以下文武百僚就德壽殿下拜箋稱賀以俟，皇帝服履袍乘輦還內。
units.en: Next civil and military officials from the Grand Preceptor downward, below Deshou Hall, bowed and submitted letters of congratulation to wait. The emperor, wearing court robes, rode the imperial carriage and returned to the inner palace.
units.literal: Next civil and military officials of the hundred ranks from the Grand Preceptor downward, below Deshou Hall, bowed and submitted letters of congratulation to wait; the emperor, wearing court robes, rode the imperial carriage and returned within.

units.zh: 十六日，宰臣率文武百僚詣文德殿拜表 稱賀。
units.en: On the sixteenth day chief ministers led all civil and military officials to Wende Hall to bow and submit congratulatory memorials.
units.literal: On the sixteenth day, chief ministers led civil and military officials of the hundred ranks to proceed to Wende Hall, bow, and present memorials of congratulation.

units.zh: 戊辰，以韓琦守司空兼侍中，曾公亮行門下侍郎兼吏部尚書、進封英國公，文彥博行尚書左僕射、檢校司徒兼中書令，富弼改武甯軍節度使、進封鄭國公，曹佾改昭慶軍節度使、檢校太傅，張昪改河陽三城節度使，宗諤同中書門下平章事，改集慶軍節度使、檢校尚書左僕射，歐陽修、趙槩並加尚書左丞，仍參知政事，陳升之爲戶部侍郎，呂公弼爲刑部侍郎，允弼、允良並加守太保，弟東陽郡王顥進封昌王，鄠國公頵進封樂安郡王。
units.en: On wuchen the cabinet was reshaped: Han Qi, Zeng Gongliang, Wen Yanbo, Fu Bi, Cao Yi, Zhang Sheng, Zongnu, Ouyang Xiu, Zhao Gai, Chen Shengzhi, Lü Gongbi, and the princes received new ranks and posts.
units.literal: Day wuchen: Han Qi kept minister of works with palace attendant; Zeng Gongliang acting vice director of the Chancellery with personnel minister, advanced Duke of Ying; Wen Yanbo acting left vice director with inspection grand mentor and concurrent director of the Secretariat; Fu Bi changed to Wuning command and Duke of Zheng; Cao Yi changed to Zhaoqing command and grand mentor; Zhang Sheng changed to Heyang command; Zongnu co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery, Jiqing command, inspection left vice director; Ouyang Xiu and Zhao Gai both added left vice director and participating administrator; Chen Shengzhi personnel vice minister; Lü Gongbi punishment vice minister; Yunbi and Yunliang both added acting grand guardian; brother Prince of Dongyang Hao advanced Prince of Chang; Prince of E Yun advanced Prince of Le’an.

units.zh: 壬寅，以曾公亮爲尚書左僕射，文彥博爲司空。
units.en: On renyin, Zeng Gongliang became left vice director and Wen Yanbo minister of works.
units.literal: Day renyin: Zeng Gongliang was made left vice director; Wen Yanbo was made minister of works.

units.zh: 丁亥，命宰臣曾公亮等極言闕失。
units.en: On dinghai, Zeng Gongliang's cabinet was commanded to name every fault.
units.literal: Day dinghai: chief ministers Zeng Gongliang and others were ordered to speak freely on omissions.

units.zh: 戊申，宰臣富弼、曾公亮以旱上表待罪，詔不允。
units.en: On wushen, Fu Bi and Zeng Gongliang offered resignations over drought; refused.
units.literal: Day wushen: chief ministers Fu Bi and Zeng Gongliang submitted guilt memorials over drought; edict refused.

units.zh: 癸丑，命曾公亮爲西京奏安仁宗、英宗御容禮儀使。
units.en: On guichou, Zeng Gongliang oversaw Western Capital portrait rites.
units.literal: Day guichou: Zeng Gongliang was made ritual commissioner for installing Renzong and Yingzong portraits at the Western Capital.

units.zh: 己丑，韓琦上《仁宗實錄》，曾公亮上《英宗實錄》。
units.en: On jichou, Renzong's and Yingzong's Veritable Records were submitted.
units.literal: Day jichou: Han Qi presented Veritable Records of Renzong; Zeng Gongliang presented Veritable Records of Yingzong.

units.zh: 伏願陛下哀忠念舊，愛孤恤寡，矜愚嘉善，舍過記功，敦骨肉之情，廣寬仁之路，思堯、舜之風，慕禹、湯之德，克己復禮，以成美化，天下幸甚。」
units.en: I venture to hope Your Majesty will pity the loyal and remember the old, cherish the orphaned and comfort the widowed, pity the foolish and praise the good, pardon faults and record merit, thicken kinship among flesh and bone, broaden the path of generous forbearance, think of the manner of Yao and Shun, admire the virtue of Yu and Tang, restrain yourself and return to ritual to complete a transformation of culture — all under Heaven would be greatly blessed."
units.literal: I venture to hope Your Majesty will pity the loyal and remember the old, cherish the orphaned and comfort the widowed, pity the foolish and praise the good, pardon faults and record merit, thicken kinship among flesh and bone, broaden the path of generous forbearance, think of the manner of Yao and Shun, admire the virtue of Yu and Tang, restrain yourself and return to ritual, to complete a transformation of culture — all under Heaven would be greatly blessed."

units.zh: 大學士李賢言：「公恂，至聖後，贊善司馬恂，宋大賢溫國公光後，宜輔導太子。」
units.en: Grand Secretary Li Xian said: "Gongxun descends from the Supreme Sage; Instructor Sima Xun descends from the great Song worthy Sima Guang, Duke of Wen—they are fit to tutor the crown prince."
units.literal: Grand Secretary Li Xian said: "Gongxun is a descendant of the Supreme Sage; Instructor Sima Xun is a descendant of the great Song worthy, Duke of Wen, Guang; they should guide the crown prince."

units.zh: 三月癸亥，宋主曙殂，子頊嗣位，遣使告哀；
units.en: On guihai day of the third month Song ruler Shu died; his son Xiang succeeded; envoys were dispatched to announce the mourning;
units.literal: Third month, on guihai day Song ruler Shu died; his son Xiang succeeded; envoys were dispatched to announce the mourning;

units.zh: 戊午，皇太叔重元與其子楚國王涅魯古及陳國王陳六、同知北院樞密使事蕭胡睹、衛王貼不、林牙涅剌溥古、統軍使蕭叠裏得、駙馬都尉參及弟術者、圖骨、旗鼓拽剌詳穩耶律郭九、文班太保奚叔、內藏提點烏骨、護衛左太保敵不古、按答、副宮使韓家奴、寶神奴等凡四百人，誘脅弩手軍犯行宮。
units.en: On wuwu day the imperial uncle Chongyuan with his son Prince of Chu Nielugu, Prince of Chen Chenliu, associate Northern Court privy commissioner Xiao Hudu, Prince of Wei Tiebu, linya Nielu Pugu, supreme commander Xiao Dielide, imperial son-in-law Can and his younger brother Muzhe, Tugu, drum-and-banner zhala detail-stable Yelü Guojiu, civil-class grand guardian Xi Shu, inner treasury intendant Wugu, Defender of the Left grand guardian Dibugu, Andada, deputy palace commissioner Han Jianu, Baoshennu, and others totaling four hundred men coerced crossbow troops to attack the mobile palace.
units.literal: On wuwu day the imperial uncle Chongyuan with his son Prince of Chu Nielugu, Prince of Chen Chenliu, associate Northern Court privy commissioner Xiao Hudu, Prince of Wei Tiebu, linya Nielu Pugu, supreme commander Xiao Dielide, imperial son-in-law Can and his younger brother Muzhe, Tugu, drum-and-banner zhala detail-stable Yelü Guojiu, civil-class grand guardian Xi Shu, inner treasury intendant Wugu, Defender of the Left grand guardian Dibugu, Andada, deputy palace commissioner Han Jianu, Baoshennu, and others totaling four hundred men coerced crossbow troops to attack the mobile palace.

units.zh: 履冰又上奏曰：臣聞夫婦之道，人倫之始。尊卑法於天地，動靜合於陰陽，陰陽和而天地生成，夫婦正而人倫式序。自家刑國，牝雞無晨，四德之禮不愆，三從之義斯在。即《喪服四制》云：「天無二日，土無二王，國無二君，家無二尊，以一理之也。故父在為母服周者，見無二尊也。」准舊儀，父在為母一週除靈，再周心喪。父必三年而後娶者，達子之志焉。豈先聖無情於所生，固有意於家國者矣。原夫上元肇年，則天已潛秉政，將圖僭篡，預自崇先。請升慈愛之喪，以抗尊嚴之禮，雖齊斬之儀不改，而几筵之制遂同。數年之間，尚未通用。天皇晏駕，中宗蒙塵。垂拱之末，果行聖母之偽符；載初之元，遂啟易代之深釁。孝和雖名反正，韋氏復效晨鳴。孝和非意暴崩，韋氏旋即稱制。不蒙陛下英算，宗廟何由克復？《易》云：「臣弒其君，子弒其父，非一朝一夕之故。」其斯之謂矣。臣謹尋禮意，防杜實深，若不早圖刊正，何以垂戒於後？所以薄言禮教，請依舊章，恩敕通明，蒙付所司詳議。且臣所獻者，蓋請正夫婦之綱，豈忘母子之道。諸議多不討其本源，所非議者，大凡只論罔極之恩；喪也寧戚；禽獸識母而不識父；秦燔書後禮經殘缺，後儒纘集，不足可憑；豈得與伯叔母服同，豈得與姑姊妹制等；三王不相襲禮，五帝不相沿樂；齊斬足為升降，歲年何忍不同：此並道聽途說之言，未習先王之旨，又安足以議經邦理俗之禮乎？臣請據經義以明之。所云「罔極之恩」者，春秋祭祀，以時思之。君子有終身之憂，霜露之感，豈止一二周之服哉！故聖人恐有朝死而夕忘，曾鳥獸之不若，為立中制，使賢不肖共成文理而已。所云「喪也寧戚」者，孔子答林放之問。至如太奢太儉，太易太戚，皆非禮中。苟不得中，名為俱失，不如太儉太戚焉。毀而滅性，猶愈於朝死夕忘焉。此論臨喪哀毀之容，豈比於同宗異姓之服？所云「禽獸識母而不識父」者，禽獸群居而聚筜，而無家國之禮，少雖知親愛其母，長不解尊嚴其父。引此為諭則亦禽獸之不若乎！所云「秦燔書後禮經殘缺，後儒纘集，不足可憑」者，人間或有遺逸，豈亦家戶到而燔之？假若盡燔，苟不可信，則墳黃都謬，庠序徒立，非聖之談，復云安屬？所云「與伯叔姑姊服同」者，伯叔姑姊有筵杖之制、三年心喪乎？所云「五帝不相沿樂，不相襲禮」，誠哉是言！此是則天懷私苞禍之情，豈可復相沿樂襲禮乎？所云「齊斬足為升降」者，母齊父斬，不易之禮。按《三年問》云：「將由修飾之君子與，三年之喪，若駟之過隙，遂之，則是無窮也。然則何以周也？曰：至親以周斷。是何也？曰：天地則已易矣，四時則已變矣，其在天地之者，莫不更始焉，以是象之也。然則何以三年？曰：加重焉耳。」故父加至再周，父在為母加三年心喪。今者還同父沒之制，則尊厭之律安施？《喪服四制》又曰：「凡禮之大體，體天地，法四時，則陰陽，順人情，故謂之禮。」訾之者是不知禮之所由生。非徒不識禮之所由制，亦恐未達孝子之通義。臣謹按《孝經》，以明陛下孝治之合至德要道，請論世欲訾禮之徒。夫至德謂孝悌，要道謂禮樂。「移風易俗，莫善於樂，安上治民，莫善於禮。」又《禮》有「無體之禮，無聲之樂。」按《孝經援神契》云：「天子孝曰就，就之為言成也。天子德被天下，澤及萬物，始終成就，則其親獲安，故曰就也。諸侯孝曰度，度者法也。諸侯居國，能奉天子法度，得不危溢，則其親獲安，故曰度也。卿大夫孝曰譽，譽之為言名也。卿大夫言行佈滿，能無惡稱，譽達遐邇，則其親獲安，故曰譽也。士孝曰究，究者以明審為義。士始升朝，辭親入仕，能審資父事君之禮，則其親獲安，故曰究也。庶人孝曰畜，畜者含畜為義。庶人含情受朴，躬耕力作，以畜其德，則其親獲安，故曰畜也。」陛下以韋氏構逆，中宗降禍，宸衷哀憤，睿情卓烈。初無一旅之眾，遂殄九重之妖，定社稷於阽危，拯宗枝於塗炭。此陛下孝悌之至，通於神明，光於四海，無所不通。使諸侯得守其法度，卿大夫得盡其言行，士得資親以事君，庶人得用天而分地。此陛下無體之禮，以安上理人也。上元以來，政由武氏，文明之後，法在凶人。賊害宗親，誅滅良善，勳階歲累，酺赦年頻。佞之則榮華，正之則遷謫。神龍、景雲之際，其事尤繁；先天、開元之間，斯弊都革。此陛下之無聲之樂，以移風易俗也。臣前狀單略，議者未識臣之懇誠。謹具狀重進，請付中書門下商量處分。臣言若讜，然敢側足於軒墀；臣言不忠，伏請竄跡於荒裔。
units.en: Lu Lubing again submitted a memorial: Your servant has heard that the way of husband and wife is the beginning of human relations. Honored and lowly take law from Heaven and earth; movement and stillness accord with yin and yang. When yin and yang are harmonious, Heaven and earth generate and complete; when husband and wife are correct, human relations are thereby ordered. From regulating the family to governing the state, the hen has no morning cry; the rites of the four virtues do not fail, and the obligation of the three followings is here. The Four Mourning Systems says: "Heaven has no two suns, earth has no two kings, the state has no two rulers, and the household has no two honored ones; these are ordered by one principle. Therefore when the father is alive, one wears one-year mourning for the mother, showing that there are not two honored ones." According to the old ritual, when the father was alive, for the mother one removed the spirit seat after one cycle and observed inner mourning for two cycles. That the father must wait three years before marrying again expresses the son's intent. How could the former sages have had no feeling for the one who gave birth, when they were certainly intent on household and state? Looking back, in the first year of Shangyuan, Zetian had already secretly taken hold of government. Planning usurpation, she first honored her ancestors. She requested raising compassionate mourning to oppose the rites of reverence; although the forms of trimmed and unhemmed mourning were not changed, the system of mats and seats became the same. For several years it still was not generally used. The Heavenly Emperor died, and Zhongzong suffered dust and exile. At the end of Chuigong, the false tally of the Sage Mother was indeed carried out; in the first year of Zaichu, the deep provocation for changing dynasties was opened. Although Xiaohe was called a return to correctness, the Wei clan again imitated the morning cry. Xiaohe suddenly died contrary to expectation, and the Wei clan immediately took charge. Had it not been for Your Majesty's heroic planning, how could the ancestral temples have been restored? The Changes says: "When a minister murders his ruler or a son murders his father, it is not the cause of one morning or one evening." This is what it means. Your servant has carefully sought the meaning of ritual, and its guard and prevention are truly deep. If we do not early plan to cut and correct this, how can we transmit warning to later times? Therefore I briefly spoke of ritual teaching and requested following the old statutes. The gracious edict was penetrating and clear, and I received referral to the responsible offices for detailed deliberation. What your servant submitted was a request to correct the bond of husband and wife; how could it forget the way of mother and son? Most deliberations do not examine the root and source. What they criticize generally only discusses boundless grace, that in mourning one should prefer grief, that birds and beasts know their mothers but not their fathers, that after Qin burned the books the ritual classics were damaged and later Confucians compiled them and are not reliable, that how could it be the same mourning as for paternal uncles' wives, how could it equal the rules for paternal aunts and sisters, that the Three Kings did not inherit one another's rites and the Five Emperors did not follow one another in music, and that trimmed and unhemmed garments are enough for increase and reduction while one cannot bear for the years to differ. These are all words heard on the road, not practiced in the former kings' intent. How are they enough to discuss the rites that order the state and regulate custom? Your servant requests to rely on classic meaning to clarify it. As for what is called "boundless grace," spring and autumn sacrifices remember it by season. A gentleman has lifelong grief and the feeling of frost and dew; how could it stop with one or two cycles of mourning dress? Therefore sages feared that some would have a morning death and evening forgetfulness, worse than birds and beasts, and established a middle regulation, so that worthy and unworthy together completed pattern and principle. As for what is called "in mourning, prefer grief," this is Confucius answering Lin Fang's question. As for too extravagant and too frugal, too easy and too grief-stricken, all are not within the ritual mean. If one cannot attain the mean, both are called losses, though too frugal and too grief-stricken are better. Destroying oneself and extinguishing one's nature is still better than morning death and evening forgetfulness. This discusses the appearance of grief and self-damage when facing mourning; how can it be compared to mourning dress for the same lineage and different surnames? As for "birds and beasts know the mother but not the father," birds and beasts live in flocks and gather without the rites of household and state. When young, they may know to love their mothers, but when grown they do not understand honoring their fathers. If this is cited as an analogy, are we not worse than birds and beasts? As for "after Qin burned the books, the ritual classics were damaged, and later Confucians compiled them, so they cannot be relied upon," among people there may have been texts left or lost; did Qin burn them from house to house? Suppose they were all burned. If they cannot be trusted, then the ancient classics are all mistaken, schools stand in vain, and to what does talk that rejects the sages belong? As for "the same mourning as paternal uncles' wives and paternal aunts and sisters," do paternal uncles' wives, paternal aunts, and sisters have a system of mats and staffs or three years of inner mourning? As for "the Five Emperors did not follow one another in music and did not inherit one another's rites," true indeed are these words! This was Zetian's feeling of harboring selfishness and wrapping disaster; how could one again follow her music and inherit her rite? As for "trimmed and unhemmed are enough for increase and reduction," trimmed for mother and unhemmed for father is unchanging ritual. According to Questions on Three Years: "Is it because of cultivated gentlemen? Three years of mourning is like a team of four horses passing a crack; if one extended it, it would be endless. Then why stop with one year? It says: the closest kin are cut off by a year. Why is this? It says: Heaven and earth have already changed; the four seasons have already changed; among what is within Heaven and earth, nothing has not begun anew, and this is used to model it. Then why three years? It says: weight is added." Therefore for the father it is increased to two full cycles, and while the father is alive, for the mother it is increased by three years of inner mourning. If now it is returned to the rule for when the father has died, where will the law of honored suppression be applied? The Four Mourning Systems also says: "In general, the great body of ritual embodies Heaven and earth, takes law from the four seasons, follows yin and yang, and accords with human feeling; therefore it is called ritual." Those who criticize this do not know from what ritual is born. Not only do they not understand from what ritual is made; I also fear they have not grasped the general obligation of a filial son. Your servant has carefully examined the Classic of Filial Piety to make clear that Your Majesty's filial governance accords with utmost virtue and the essential way, and I request to discuss those in the age who wish to criticize ritual. Utmost virtue means filial piety and fraternal respect; the essential way means rites and music. "For changing customs, nothing is better than music; for securing superiors and governing the people, nothing is better than ritual." Also, the Ritual has "formless ritual and soundless music." According to the Filial Piety apocryphon Yuan Shen Qi: "The Son of Heaven's filial piety is called completion; completion means accomplishing. When the Son of Heaven's virtue covers All Under Heaven and his grace reaches the myriad things, beginning and end are accomplished, and then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called completion. A feudal lord's filial piety is called measure; measure means law. When a feudal lord resides in his state and can uphold the Son of Heaven's laws and measures, not becoming endangered or overflowing, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called measure. A minister or great officer's filial piety is called reputation; reputation means name. When a minister or great officer's words and conduct spread fully and can have no evil name, and his reputation reaches far and near, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called reputation. A shi's filial piety is called investigation; investigation takes clarity and examination as its meaning. When a shi first enters court, leaves his parents and enters service, and can examine the rite of using the father as resource to serve the ruler, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called investigation. A commoner's filial piety is called storing up; storing up takes containing and preserving as its meaning. When a commoner contains feeling and receives simplicity, personally plowing and laboring in order to store up his virtue, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called storing up." Because the Wei clan plotted rebellion and Zhongzong suffered disaster, Your Majesty's imperial heart was grieved and angered, and your sagely feeling was outstanding and fierce. At first you had not even one brigade of troops, yet you destroyed the monster in the ninefold palace, fixed the altars of soil and grain in danger, and rescued the imperial branches from mire and ashes. This is the utmost of Your Majesty's filial piety and fraternal respect, penetrating to spirits and brightness, shining over the four seas, with nothing it does not reach. It lets feudal lords keep their laws and measures, ministers and great officers exhaust their words and conduct, shi use kinship to serve the ruler, and commoners use Heaven and divide earth. This is Your Majesty's formless ritual, by which you secure superiors and order the people. Since Shangyuan, government came from the Wu clan; after Wenming, law lay with cruel people. They harmed imperial kin, killed the good, accumulated merit ranks every year, and frequently held feasts and amnesties. To flatter them brought glory; to correct them brought demotion and exile. During Shenlong and Jingyun, these affairs were especially numerous; between Xiantian and Kaiyuan, these abuses were all reformed. This is Your Majesty's soundless music, by which you changed customs. Your servant's previous statement was brief, and the debaters did not understand my earnest sincerity. I have carefully prepared this statement and present it again, requesting that it be sent to the Secretariat-Chancellery for deliberation and disposition. If your servant's words are honest, then I dare stand beside the palace steps. If your servant's words are not loyal, I humbly request exile to the distant borders.

Honored and lowly take law from Heaven and earth; movement and stillness accord with yin and yang. When yin and yang are harmonious, Heaven and earth generate and complete; when husband and wife are correct, human relations are thereby ordered. From regulating the family to governing the state, the hen has no morning cry; the rites of the four virtues do not fail, and the obligation of the three followings is here. The Four Mourning Systems says: "Heaven has no two suns, earth has no two kings, the state has no two rulers, and the household has no two honored ones; these are ordered by one principle. Therefore when the father is alive, one wears one-year mourning for the mother, showing that there are not two honored ones." According to the old ritual, when the father was alive, for the mother one removed the spirit seat after one cycle and observed inner mourning for two cycles. That the father must wait three years before marrying again expresses the son's intent. How could the former sages have had no feeling for the one who gave birth, when they were certainly intent on household and state? Looking back, in the first year of Shangyuan, Zetian had already secretly taken hold of government. Planning usurpation, she first honored her ancestors. She requested raising compassionate mourning to oppose the rites of reverence; although the forms of trimmed and unhemmed mourning were not changed, the system of mats and seats became the same. For several years it still was not generally used. The Heavenly Emperor died, and Zhongzong suffered dust and exile. At the end of Chuigong, the false tally of the Sage Mother was indeed carried out; in the first year of Zaichu, the deep provocation for changing dynasties was opened. Although Xiaohe was called a return to correctness, the Wei clan again imitated the morning cry. Xiaohe suddenly died contrary to expectation, and the Wei clan immediately took charge. Had it not been for Your Majesty's heroic planning, how could the ancestral temples have been restored? The Changes says: "When a minister murders his ruler or a son murders his father, it is not the cause of one morning or one evening." This is what it means. Your servant has carefully sought the meaning of ritual, and its guard and prevention are truly deep. If we do not early plan to cut and correct this, how can we transmit warning to later times? Therefore I briefly spoke of ritual teaching and requested following the old statutes. The gracious edict was penetrating and clear, and I received referral to the responsible offices for detailed deliberation. What your servant submitted was a request to correct the bond of husband and wife; how could it forget the way of mother and son? Most deliberations do not examine the root and source. What they criticize generally only discusses boundless grace, that in mourning one should prefer grief, that birds and beasts know their mothers but not their fathers, that after Qin burned the books the ritual classics were damaged and later Confucians compiled them and are not reliable, that how could it be the same mourning as for paternal uncles' wives, how could it equal the rules for paternal aunts and sisters, that the Three Kings did not inherit one another's rites and the Five Emperors did not follow one another in music, and that trimmed and unhemmed garments are enough for increase and reduction while one cannot bear for the years to differ. These are all words heard on the road, not practiced in the former kings' intent. How are they enough to discuss the rites that order the state and regulate custom? Your servant requests to rely on classic meaning to clarify it. As for what is called "boundless grace," spring and autumn sacrifices remember it by season. A gentleman has lifelong grief and the feeling of frost and dew; how could it stop with one or two cycles of mourning dress? Therefore sages feared that some would have a morning death and evening forgetfulness, worse than birds and beasts, and established a middle regulation, so that worthy and unworthy together completed pattern and principle. As for what is called "in mourning, prefer grief," this is Confucius answering Lin Fang's question. As for too extravagant and too frugal, too easy and too grief-stricken, all are not within the ritual mean. If one cannot attain the mean, both are called losses, though too frugal and too grief-stricken are better. Destroying oneself and extinguishing one's nature is still better than morning death and evening forgetfulness. This discusses the appearance of grief and self-damage when facing mourning; how can it be compared to mourning dress for the same lineage and different surnames? As for "birds and beasts know the mother but not the father," birds and beasts live in flocks and gather without the rites of household and state. When young, they may know to love their mothers, but when grown they do not understand honoring their fathers. If this is cited as an analogy, are we not worse than birds and beasts? As for "after Qin burned the books, the ritual classics were damaged, and later Confucians compiled them, so they cannot be relied upon," among people there may have been texts left or lost; did Qin burn them from house to house? Suppose they were all burned. If they cannot be trusted, then the ancient classics are all mistaken, schools stand in vain, and to what does talk that rejects the sages belong? As for "the same mourning as paternal uncles' wives and paternal aunts and sisters," do paternal uncles' wives, paternal aunts, and sisters have a system of mats and staffs or three years of inner mourning? As for "the Five Emperors did not follow one another in music and did not inherit one another's rites," true indeed are these words! This was Zetian's feeling of harboring selfishness and wrapping disaster; how could one again follow her music and inherit her rite? As for "trimmed and unhemmed are enough for increase and reduction," trimmed for mother and unhemmed for father is unchanging ritual. According to Questions on Three Years: "Is it because of cultivated gentlemen? Three years of mourning is like a team of four horses passing a crack; if one extended it, it would be endless. Then why stop with one year? It says: the closest kin are cut off by a year. Why is this? It says: Heaven and earth have already changed; the four seasons have already changed; among what is within Heaven and earth, nothing has not begun anew, and this is used to model it. Then why three years? It says: weight is added." Therefore for the father it is increased to two full cycles, and while the father is alive, for the mother it is increased by three years of inner mourning. If now it is returned to the rule for when the father has died, where will the law of honored suppression be applied? The Four Mourning Systems also says: "In general, the great body of ritual embodies Heaven and earth, takes law from the four seasons, follows yin and yang, and accords with human feeling; therefore it is called ritual." Those who criticize this do not know from what ritual is born. Not only do they not understand from what ritual is made; I also fear they have not grasped the general obligation of a filial son. Your servant has carefully examined the Classic of Filial Piety to make clear that Your Majesty's filial governance accords with utmost virtue and the essential way, and I request to discuss those in the age who wish to criticize ritual. Utmost virtue means filial piety and fraternal respect; the essential way means rites and music. "For changing customs, nothing is better than music; for securing superiors and governing the people, nothing is better than ritual." Also, the Ritual has "formless ritual and soundless music." According to the Filial Piety apocryphon Yuan Shen Qi: "The Son of Heaven's filial piety is called completion; completion means accomplishing. When the Son of Heaven's virtue covers All Under Heaven and his grace reaches the myriad things, beginning and end are accomplished, and then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called completion. A feudal lord's filial piety is called measure; measure means law. When a feudal lord resides in his state and can uphold the Son of Heaven's laws and measures, not becoming endangered or overflowing, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called measure. A minister or great officer's filial piety is called reputation; reputation means name. When a minister or great officer's words and conduct spread fully and can have no evil name, and his reputation reaches far and near, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called reputation. A shi's filial piety is called investigation; investigation takes clarity and examination as its meaning. When a shi first enters court, leaves his parents and enters service, and can examine the rite of using the father as resource to serve the ruler, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called investigation. A commoner's filial piety is called storing up; storing up takes containing and preserving as its meaning. When a commoner contains feeling and receives simplicity, personally plowing and laboring in order to store up his virtue, then his parents obtain peace; therefore it is called storing up." Because the Wei clan plotted rebellion and Zhongzong suffered disaster, Your Majesty's imperial heart was grieved and angered, and your sagely feeling was outstanding and fierce. At first you had not even one brigade of troops, yet you destroyed the monster in the ninefold palace, fixed the altars of soil and grain in danger, and rescued the imperial branches from mire and ashes. This is the utmost of Your Majesty's filial piety and fraternal respect, penetrating to spirits and brightness, shining over the four seas, with nothing it does not reach. It lets feudal lords keep their laws and measures, ministers and great officers exhaust their words and conduct, shi use kinship to serve the ruler, and commoners use Heaven and divide earth. This is Your Majesty's formless ritual, by which you secure superiors and order the people. Since Shangyuan, government came from the Wu clan; after Wenming, law lay with cruel people. They harmed imperial kin, killed the good, accumulated merit ranks every year, and frequently held feasts and amnesties. To flatter them brought glory; to correct them brought demotion and exile. During Shenlong and Jingyun, these affairs were especially numerous; between Xiantian and Kaiyuan, these abuses were all reformed. This is Your Majesty's soundless music, by which you changed customs. Your servant's previous statement was brief, and the debaters did not understand my earnest sincerity. I have carefully prepared this statement and present it again, requesting that it be sent to the Secretariat-Chancellery for deliberation and disposition. If your servant's words are honest, then I dare stand beside the palace steps. If your servant's words are not loyal, I humbly request exile to the distant borders.

units.zh: 案：契丹丙午歲入汴，順數至甲子歲為十八年，實太祖乾德二年也。
units.en: Note: the Khitans entered Bian in the bingwu year; counting forward to jiazi gives eighteen years—the year Qiande 2 of Taizu.
units.literal: Note: in the Khitan year bingwu they entered Bian; counting forward to the year jiazi makes eighteen years—actually Taizu's Qiande 2.

units.zh: 庚辰，張昪罷，以文彥博爲樞密使。
units.en: On gengchen, Zhang Bian fell and Wen Yanbo took military affairs.
units.literal: Day gengchen: Zhang Bian was dismissed; Wen Yanbo was made military affairs commissioner.

units.zh: 十年十二月，以太上皇后新年七十，詔以立春日行慶賀之禮。
units.en: In the twelfth month of the tenth year, because the Retired Empress would be seventy in the new year, an edict ordered that congratulatory rites be performed on the day of the beginning of spring.
units.literal: In the twelfth month of the tenth year, because the Retired Empress would be seventy in the new year, an edict ordered that congratulatory rites be performed on the day of the beginning of spring.

units.zh: 上元元年，天后上表曰：「至如父在為母服止一期，雖心喪三年，服由尊降。
units.en: In the first year of Shangyuan, Empress Wu submitted a memorial, saying: "As for when the father is alive, mourning for the mother stops at one cycle—though heart mourning is three years, the garment is reduced by reverence for the father.
units.literal: In the first year of Shangyuan, Empress Wu submitted a memorial, saying: "As for when the father is alive, mourning for the mother stops at one cycle—though heart mourning is three years, the garment is reduced by reverence for the father.

units.zh: 則天皇后請同父沒之服，三年然始除靈。
units.en: Empress Wu had asked for the same garment as when the father was dead—three years before tablet removal.
units.literal: Empress Wu Zetian requested mourning the same as when the father is dead—three years before removal of the spirit tablet.

units.zh: 高宗下詔，依議行焉，
units.en: Gaozong decreed and put her proposal into practice.
units.literal: Gaozong issued a decree and followed the proposal in practice,

units.zh: 至垂拱年中，始編入格，易代之後，俗乃通行。
units.en: Only in Chuigong was it written into the code; after the dynastic shift the custom spread.
units.literal: By the Chuigong era it was first entered into the administrative code; after the change of dynasty the custom then spread in practice.

units.zh: 竊謂子之於母，慈愛特深，非母不生，非母不育。
units.en: A child owes the mother a singular depth of love: without her there is no birth, without her no rearing.
units.literal: I venture to say that in a child's relation to the mother, affection is especially deep—without the mother one is not born, without the mother one is not reared.

units.zh: 推燥居濕，咽苦吐甘，生養勞瘁，恩斯極矣！
units.en: She tended his dryness and wetness, swallowed bitterness and gave sweetness—the labor of nurture exhausts what kindness can mean.
units.literal: Tending dryness and wetness, swallowing bitterness and spitting sweetness—the toil of bearing and rearing, kindness reaches its utmost!

units.zh: 所以禽獸之情，猶知其母，三年在懷，理宜崇報。
units.en: Even beasts know their dam; three years in the womb demand a commensurate return.
units.literal: Therefore even beasts in feeling know their mother; three years in the womb—by principle one ought to honor her in return.

units.zh: 若父在為母服止一期，尊父之敬雖周，報母之慈有闕。
units.en: Stopping at one cycle while the father lived honored him fully but left the mother's kindness short.
units.literal: If when the father is alive mourning for the mother stops at one cycle, reverence for the father is complete yet requital of the mother's kindness is lacking.

units.zh: 且齊斬之制，足為差減，更令周以一期，恐傷人子之志。
units.en: Hemmed sackcloth already graded the mourning; shrinking three years to one cycle would wound a son's intent.
units.literal: Moreover the hemmed-and-cut garment system is sufficient for graduated reduction; to make one cycle suffice where three years should apply would wound the son's intent.

units.zh: 今請父在為母終三年之服。」
units.en: We now request that when the father is alive mourning for the mother run the full three years."
units.literal: We now request that when the father is alive mourning for the mother run the full three years."

units.zh: 刑部郎中田再思建議曰：干尊坤卑，天一地二，陰陽之位分矣，夫婦之道配焉。至若死喪之威，隆殺之等，禮經五服之制，齊斬有殊，考妣三年之喪，貴賤無隔，以報免懷之慈，以酬罔極之恩者也。稽之上古，喪期無數，暨乎中葉，方有歲年。《禮》云：「五帝殊時，不相沿樂；三王異代，不相襲禮。」《白虎通》云：「質文再變，正朔三而復。」自周公制禮之後，孔父刊經已來，爰殊厭降之儀，以標服紀之節。重輕從俗，斟酌隨時。故知禮不從天而降，不由地而出也，在人消息，為適時之中耳。春秋諸國，魯最知禮，以周公之後，孔子之邦也。晉韓起來聘，言「周禮盡在魯矣。」齊仲孫來盟，言「魯猶秉周禮。」尚有子張問高宗諒陰三年，子思不聽其子服出母，子游謂同母異父昆弟之服大功，子夏謂合從齊衰之制。此等並四科之數，十哲之人，高步孔門，親承聖訓，及遇喪事，猶此致疑，即明自古已來，升降不一者也。三年之制，說者紛然。鄭玄以為二十七月，王肅以為二十五月。又改葬之服，鄭云服緦三月，王云訖葬而除。又繼母出嫁，鄭云皆服，王云從於繼育，乃為之服。又無服之殤，鄭云子生一月，哭之一日；王云以哭之一日易服之月。鄭、王祖經宗傳，各有異同；荀摯采古求遺，互為損益。方知去聖漸遠，殘缺彌多。故曰會禮之家，名為聚訟，寧有定哉！而父在為母三年，行之已逾四紀，出自高宗大帝之代，不從則天皇后之朝。大帝御極之辰，中宮獻書之日，往時參議，將可施行，編之於格，服之已久。前王所是，疏而為律；後王所是，著而為令。何必乖先帝之旨，阻人子之情，虧純孝之心，背德義之本？有何妨於聖化，有何紊於彝倫，而欲服之週年，與伯叔母齊焉，與姑姊妹同焉？夫三年之喪，如白駒之過隙，君子喪親，有終身之憂，何況再周乎！夫禮者，體也，履也，示之以跡。孝者，畜也，養也，因之以心。小人不恥不仁，不畏不義。服之有制，使愚人企及；衣之以衰，使見之摧痛。以此防人，人猶有朝死而夕忘者；以此制人，人猶有釋服而從吉者。方今漸歸古樸，須敦孝義，抑賢引愚，理資寧戚，食稻衣錦，所不忍聞。若以庶事朝儀，一依周禮，則古之人臣見君也，公卿大夫贄羔雁、珪璧，今何故不依乎？周之用刑也，墨、劓、宮、刖，今何故不行乎？周則侯、甸、男、衛，朝聘有數，今何故不行乎？周則不五十不仕，七十不入朝，今何故不依乎？周則井、邑、丘、甸，以立徵稅，今何故不行乎？周則三老五等，父死子及，今何故不行乎？周則冠冕衣裘，乘車而戰，今何故不行乎？周則分土五更，膠序養老，今何故不行乎？諸如此例，不可勝述。何獨孝思之事，愛一年之服於其母乎？可為痛心，可為慟哭者！《詩》云：「哀哀父母，生我劬勞。」《禮》云：「父之親子也，親賢而下無能；母之親子也，賢則親之，無能則憐之。」阮嗣宗晉代之英才，方外之高士，以為母重於父。據齊斬升數，粗細已降，何忍服之節制，減至於周？豈後代之士，盡慚於古。循古未必是，依今未必非也。又同爨服緦，禮經明義。嫂叔遠別，同諸路人。引而進之，觸類而長。猶子咸衣苴枲，季父不服緦麻，推遠之情有餘，睦親之義未足。又母之昆弟，情切渭陽，翟酺訟舅之冤，甯氏宅甥之相，我之出也，義亦殷焉。不同從母之尊，遂降小功之服，依諸古禮，有爽俗情。今貶舅而宗姨，是陋今而榮古。此並太宗之制也，行之百年矣，輒為刊復，實用有疑。
units.en: Tian Zaisi, Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice, made a proposal: Qian is honored and kun is lowly; Heaven is one and earth is two. The positions of yin and yang are divided, and the way of husband and wife is paired with them. As for the awe of death and mourning and the grades of fullness and reduction, the ritual classics have the system of the five mourning grades. Trimmed and unhemmed mourning differ, but the three-year mourning for father and mother has no barrier between noble and base, because it repays the kindness of bearing and cherishing and answers boundless grace. Examining high antiquity, mourning terms had no fixed number; by middle antiquity, only then were there years and months. The Ritual says: "The Five Emperors differed in time and did not follow one another in music; the Three Kings differed in age and did not inherit one another's rites." The Baihu Tong says: "Plainness and refinement change twice, and the first month changes through three and returns." Since the Duke of Zhou made ritual and since Confucius edited the classics, there have been different rules of suppression and reduction to mark the divisions of mourning regulations. Heavy and light follow custom; deliberation and adjustment follow the time. Thus we know ritual does not descend from Heaven or come out from earth; it lies in human increase and decrease, making what fits the time and the mean. Among the states of the Spring and Autumn, Lu best knew ritual, because it was the descendants of the Duke of Zhou and the state of Confucius. When Han Qi of Jin came on a visit, he said, "The rites of Zhou are all in Lu." When Zhongsun of Qi came to make a covenant, he said, "Lu still holds the rites of Zhou." Yet Zizhang asked about Gaozong's three years of silent mourning; Zisi did not allow his son to wear mourning for his divorced mother; Ziyou said that brothers with the same mother but different fathers should wear great-work mourning; Zixia said they should follow the trimmed-mourning rule. These were all among the numbered disciples of the four categories and the ten philosophers, men of high rank in Confucius's gate who personally received the sage teaching; yet when they encountered mourning matters, they still produced doubts like this. This makes clear that since antiquity increases and reductions have not been uniform. As for the three-year system, explanations are confused. Zheng Xuan considered it twenty-seven months; Wang Su considered it twenty-five months. Again for mourning after reburial, Zheng says one wears fine hemp for three months, while Wang says one removes it when burial is completed. Again for a stepmother who remarries, Zheng says all wear mourning, while Wang says that only if one followed and was raised by her does one wear mourning. Again for a child who died young and for whom there is no mourning, Zheng says that for a child born one month, one cries one day; Wang says one day of crying replaces one month of mourning. Zheng and Wang each take the classics as ancestor and the commentaries as lineage, and each has differences. Xun Zhi collected antiquity and sought what was left, alternately reducing and increasing. From this we know that as the sages recede farther away, gaps and losses become more numerous. Therefore it is said that houses that assemble ritual are called gathered lawsuits; how could there be a fixed answer? Yet the three-year mourning for a mother while the father is alive has been practiced for more than forty years. It came from the generation of Gaozong the Great Emperor, not from the court of Empress Zetian. When the Great Emperor ruled and the palace submitted the document, the former deliberations could be put into practice; it was compiled into the regulations, and the mourning has been worn for a long time. What a former king approved was set out as law; what a later king approved was written as ordinance. Why must we oppose the former emperor's intent, block the feeling of a person's son, diminish a pure filial heart, and turn against the root of virtue and obligation? What harm is there to sage transformation? What disorder is there to the constant human order, that one would make the mourning one year, equal to that for paternal uncles' wives, and the same as for paternal aunts and sisters? The three-year mourning passes like a white colt through a crack; a gentleman mourning his parent has lifelong grief, how much more for two full cycles! Ritual is embodiment, practice, showing it by traces. Filial piety is storing up, nourishing, following it by the heart. Petty people are not ashamed of inhumanity and do not fear unrighteousness. Mourning dress has regulations to make foolish people reach upward; they are clothed in mourning garments so that seeing them produces crushing pain. Using this to guard people, there are still those who forget by evening one who died in the morning. Using this to regulate people, there are still those who remove mourning and follow auspicious affairs. Now we are gradually returning to ancient simplicity and must deepen filial piety and obligation. Restraining the worthy and drawing in the foolish, in principle, depends on Ning Qi; eating rice and wearing brocade are things one cannot bear to hear. If ordinary affairs and court ceremony are all to follow the Zhou rites, then when ancient ministers saw the ruler, dukes, ministers, and great officers presented lambs, geese, jade tablets, and disks; why do we not follow this now? Zhou punishments used tattooing, nose-cutting, castration, and foot-cutting; why do we not carry them out now? Zhou had hou, dian, nan, and wei domains, and audiences and visits had fixed numbers; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou did not let one serve before fifty, and at seventy one did not enter court; why do we not follow this now? Zhou used jing, yi, qiu, and dian to establish taxation; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou had three elders and five grades, father dying and son succeeding; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou used caps, robes, fur garments, and chariots in battle; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou divided land and had five geng, and in village and school nourished the aged; why do we not carry this out now? Examples such as these cannot be fully stated. Why only in the matter of filial thought begrudge one year of mourning for one's mother? This can make the heart ache; this can make one wail. The Odes says: "Alas, alas, my father and mother, who bore me with toil." The Ritual says: "When a father loves his child, he loves the worthy and lowers the incapable; when a mother loves her child, if worthy she loves him, and if incapable she pities him." Ruan Sizong, an outstanding talent of Jin and lofty man beyond the world, considered the mother weightier than the father. Based on the thread counts of trimmed and unhemmed mourning, coarseness and fineness already descend. How can one bear for the term of mourning to be reduced to one year? Surely later men are not all ashamed before antiquity. Following antiquity is not necessarily right; following the present is not necessarily wrong. Again, those who share the cooking hearth wear fine hemp; this is a clear meaning of the ritual classics. Elder-brother's wife and younger-brother-in-law are kept distant and treated like people on the road. Drawing them in and advancing them extends by analogy. Nephews all wear hemp mourning, but a younger uncle does not wear fine hemp; the feeling of pushing away is more than enough, and the obligation of harmonizing kin is insufficient. Again the mother's brothers have feeling as close as Weiyang; Di Pu litigated his uncle's injustice, and the Ning family housed a nephew as minister. Since I come from them, obligation too is deep. Not sharing the honor of a mother's sister, they are thereby lowered to small-work mourning. According to the ancient rites, this conflicts with common feeling. Now lowering the maternal uncle while honoring the maternal aunt is to scorn the present and glorify antiquity. These are all Taizong's regulations and have been practiced for a hundred years; rashly cutting and restoring them truly creates doubt.
