Thus we know ritual does not descend from Heaven or come out from earth; it lies in human increase and decrease, making what fits the time and the mean. Among the states of the Spring and Autumn, Lu best knew ritual, because it was the descendants of the Duke of Zhou and the state of Confucius. When Han Qi of Jin came on a visit, he said, "The rites of Zhou are all in Lu." When Zhongsun of Qi came to make a covenant, he said, "Lu still holds the rites of Zhou." Yet Zizhang asked about Gaozong's three years of silent mourning; Zisi did not allow his son to wear mourning for his divorced mother; Ziyou said that brothers with the same mother but different fathers should wear great-work mourning; Zixia said they should follow the trimmed-mourning rule. These were all among the numbered disciples of the four categories and the ten philosophers, men of high rank in Confucius's gate who personally received the sage teaching; yet when they encountered mourning matters, they still produced doubts like this. This makes clear that since antiquity increases and reductions have not been uniform. As for the three-year system, explanations are confused. Zheng Xuan considered it twenty-seven months; Wang Su considered it twenty-five months. Again for mourning after reburial, Zheng says one wears fine hemp for three months, while Wang says one removes it when burial is completed. Again for a stepmother who remarries, Zheng says all wear mourning, while Wang says that only if one followed and was raised by her does one wear mourning. Again for a child who died young and for whom there is no mourning, Zheng says that for a child born one month, one cries one day; Wang says one day of crying replaces one month of mourning. Zheng and Wang each take the classics as ancestor and the commentaries as lineage, and each has differences. Xun Zhi collected antiquity and sought what was left, alternately reducing and increasing. From this we know that as the sages recede farther away, gaps and losses become more numerous. Therefore it is said that houses that assemble ritual are called gathered lawsuits; how could there be a fixed answer? Yet the three-year mourning for a mother while the father is alive has been practiced for more than forty years. It came from the generation of Gaozong the Great Emperor, not from the court of Empress Zetian. When the Great Emperor ruled and the palace submitted the document, the former deliberations could be put into practice; it was compiled into the regulations, and the mourning has been worn for a long time. What a former king approved was set out as law; what a later king approved was written as ordinance. Why must we oppose the former emperor's intent, block the feeling of a person's son, diminish a pure filial heart, and turn against the root of virtue and obligation? What harm is there to sage transformation? What disorder is there to the constant human order, that one would make the mourning one year, equal to that for paternal uncles' wives, and the same as for paternal aunts and sisters? The three-year mourning passes like a white colt through a crack; a gentleman mourning his parent has lifelong grief, how much more for two full cycles! Ritual is embodiment, practice, showing it by traces. Filial piety is storing up, nourishing, following it by the heart. Petty people are not ashamed of inhumanity and do not fear unrighteousness. Mourning dress has regulations to make foolish people reach upward; they are clothed in mourning garments so that seeing them produces crushing pain. Using this to guard people, there are still those who forget by evening one who died in the morning. Using this to regulate people, there are still those who remove mourning and follow auspicious affairs. Now we are gradually returning to ancient simplicity and must deepen filial piety and obligation. Restraining the worthy and drawing in the foolish, in principle, depends on Ning Qi; eating rice and wearing brocade are things one cannot bear to hear. If ordinary affairs and court ceremony are all to follow the Zhou rites, then when ancient ministers saw the ruler, dukes, ministers, and great officers presented lambs, geese, jade tablets, and disks; why do we not follow this now? Zhou punishments used tattooing, nose-cutting, castration, and foot-cutting; why do we not carry them out now? Zhou had hou, dian, nan, and wei domains, and audiences and visits had fixed numbers; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou did not let one serve before fifty, and at seventy one did not enter court; why do we not follow this now? Zhou used jing, yi, qiu, and dian to establish taxation; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou had three elders and five grades, father dying and son succeeding; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou used caps, robes, fur garments, and chariots in battle; why do we not carry this out now? Zhou divided land and had five geng, and in village and school nourished the aged; why do we not carry this out now? Examples such as these cannot be fully stated. Why only in the matter of filial thought begrudge one year of mourning for one's mother? This can make the heart ache; this can make one wail. The Odes says: "Alas, alas, my father and mother, who bore me with toil." The Ritual says: "When a father loves his child, he loves the worthy and lowers the incapable; when a mother loves her child, if worthy she loves him, and if incapable she pities him." Ruan Sizong, an outstanding talent of Jin and lofty man beyond the world, considered the mother weightier than the father. Based on the thread counts of trimmed and unhemmed mourning, coarseness and fineness already descend. How can one bear for the term of mourning to be reduced to one year? Surely later men are not all ashamed before antiquity. Following antiquity is not necessarily right; following the present is not necessarily wrong. Again, those who share the cooking hearth wear fine hemp; this is a clear meaning of the ritual classics. Elder-brother's wife and younger-brother-in-law are kept distant and treated like people on the road. Drawing them in and advancing them extends by analogy. Nephews all wear hemp mourning, but a younger uncle does not wear fine hemp; the feeling of pushing away is more than enough, and the obligation of harmonizing kin is insufficient. Again the mother's brothers have feeling as close as Weiyang; Di Pu litigated his uncle's injustice, and the Ning family housed a nephew as minister. Since I come from them, obligation too is deep. Not sharing the honor of a mother's sister, they are thereby lowered to small-work mourning. According to the ancient rites, this conflicts with common feeling. Now lowering the maternal uncle while honoring the maternal aunt is to scorn the present and glorify antiquity. These are all Taizong's regulations and have been practiced for a hundred years; rashly cutting and restoring them truly creates doubt.

units.zh: 上元中，則天皇后上表，請同父沒之服，亦未有行。
units.en: In Shangyuan Wu had asked for mourning equal to a father's death, but it had not yet taken effect.
units.literal: In the Shangyuan era Empress Wu Zetian submitted a memorial requesting mourning the same as when the father is dead, yet it was still not carried out.

units.zh: 執折上巾者升，掌冠者降一等受之，右執項，左執前，進皇太子席前，北向立，祝曰：“谘爾元子，肇冠於阼。
units.en: The attendant bearing the folded kerchief ascended. The crown-placer stepped down one level to receive it, grasping the rear with his right hand and the front with his left, and advanced to stand north-facing before the crown prince's seat. He pronounced the blessing: "I announce to you, eldest son, that you are first capped at the eastern steps.
units.literal: The bearer of the folded-up kerchief ascended; the crown-placer descended one step to receive it, holding the nape with his right hand and the front with his left, advanced before the crown prince's seat, stood facing north, and offered the blessing: "I announce to you, eldest son, that you are first capped at the eastern steps.

units.zh: 左輔詣御坐前，承製降東階，詣掌 冠者前西向稱有制，典儀讚在位官再拜訖，宣製曰：“皇太子冠，命卿等行禮。”
units.en: The Left Assistant approached the throne, received the edict, descended the eastern steps, and stood west-facing before the crown-placers to announce that an edict was forthcoming. After the master of ceremonies had the officials in attendance perform a double bow, the edict was read: "The crown prince is to receive his cap; I command you to conduct the ceremony."
units.literal: The Left Assistant went before the imperial seat, received the edict, descended the eastern steps, went before the crown-placers, faced west, and announced that there was an edict; the master of ceremonies had the officials in position double-bow; then the edict was proclaimed: "The crown prince is to be capped; I command you to perform the ceremony."

units.zh: 徽宗親製《冠禮沿革》十一卷，命儀禮局仿以編次。
units.en: Emperor Huizong personally compiled eleven fascicles entitled Evolution of Capping Rites and instructed the Bureau of Ceremonial to organize the ritual according to that model.
units.literal: Emperor Huizong personally composed eleven fascicles of "Evolution of Capping Rites," ordering the Bureau of Ceremonial to compile and arrange [the ceremony] according to it.

units.zh: 太子興，內侍跪進服，服訖，樂止。
units.en: The crown prince rose while inner attendants knelt to bring forward his garments. Once he was dressed, the music stopped.
units.literal: The crown prince rose; inner attendants knelt to present the garments; when he was dressed, the music ceased.

units.zh: 禮直官等引太子降自東階，樂作，由 西階升，即醴席南向坐，樂止。
units.en: Ritual officers escorted the crown prince down the eastern steps to music, then up the western steps to take his seat facing south at the ceremonial wine seat; the music stopped.
units.literal: Ritual officers and others led the crown prince down the eastern steps; music was performed; he ascended by the western steps and took his seat facing south at the ceremonial wine seat; the music ceased.

units.zh: 太常博士請再拜，太子 再拜訖，搢笏，舞蹈，再拜，奏聖躬萬福，又再拜。
units.en: An academician of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices called for a double bow. The crown prince completed it, inserted his tablet, performed the dance-bow and another double bow, reported that the Son of Heaven enjoyed ten thousand blessings, and bowed again.
units.literal: A Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician requested a double bow; the crown prince finished double-bowing, inserted his tablet, performed the dance-bow, double-bowed again, reported that the sacred person enjoyed ten thousand blessings, and double-bowed once more.

units.zh: 宣訖，太子再拜訖，禮直官等引太子前，俯伏，跪，奏稱：“臣雖不敏，敢不祗奉！”
units.en: When the proclamation ended, the crown prince completed his double bow. Ritual officers led him forward; he prostrated himself, knelt, and reported: "Though your servant is not clever, how dare he fail to obey reverently!"
units.literal: When the proclamation was finished, the crown prince finished double-bowing; ritual officers and others led the crown prince forward; he prostrated himself, knelt, and reported: "Though your servant is not clever, how dare he not reverently obey!"

units.zh: 太子入內，朝見皇后，如宮中儀。
units.en: The crown prince entered the inner palace and paid his respects to the empress according to the palace rites.
units.literal: The crown prince entered the inner quarters and paid his respects to the empress, as in the palace ceremony.

units.zh: 大晟展宮架樂於橫街南，太常設 太子冠席東階上、東宮官位於後，設褥位，陳服於席南，東領北上。
units.en: The Dasheng Music Office set up the palace frame orchestra south of the cross street. The Court of Imperial Sacrifices placed the crown prince's capping seat on the eastern steps, with positions for Eastern Palace officials behind it, a cushioned seat, and ceremonial dress laid out to the south of the seat, facing east with the leading edge to the north.
units.literal: The Dasheng Office deployed the palace frame music south of the cross street; the Court of Imperial Sacrifices set the crown prince's capping seat on the eastern steps, with Eastern Palace officials' positions behind it; a cushioned seat was set out, and garments were displayed south of the seat, aligned east-leading north-up.

units.zh: 禮直官、通事舍人、太常博士引太子詣朵殿東房。
units.en: Ritual officers, Communication Chamber attendants, and academicians of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices escorted the crown prince to the eastern room of the side hall.
units.literal: Ritual officers, Communication Chamber attendants, and Court of Imperial Sacrifices academicians led the crown prince to the eastern chamber of the side hall.

units.zh: 東宮官入，詣太子東房，次禮直官等引太子，內侍二人夾侍，東宮官後從，《欽安之樂》作，即席西向坐，樂止。
units.en: Eastern Palace officials entered and went to the crown prince's eastern room. Ritual officers then escorted the crown prince out, flanked by two inner attendants with Eastern Palace officials following behind, to the music of Qin'an. He took his seat facing west, and the music stopped.
units.literal: Eastern Palace officials entered and went to the crown prince's eastern chamber; next ritual officers and others led the crown prince, with two inner attendants attending on either side and Eastern Palace officials following behind; "Qin'an" music was performed; he took his seat facing west; the music ceased.

units.zh: 掌冠者揖太子復坐，禮直官等引掌冠者降詣罍洗，如上儀。
units.en: The crown-placer gestured for the crown prince to resume his seat, and ritual officers escorted him down to the wash basin as before.
units.literal: The crown-placer bowed to the crown prince to return to his seat; ritual officers and others led the crown-placer down to the jar and wash-basin, as in the preceding ceremony.

units.zh: 執遠遊冠者升，掌冠者降二等受之，右執項，左執前，進太子席前，北向立，祝曰：“爰即令辰，申加元服。
units.en: The attendant bearing the Cap of Distant Travels ascended. The crown-placer stepped down two levels to receive it, grasping the rear with his right hand and the front with his left, and advanced to stand north-facing before the crown prince's seat. He pronounced the blessing: "On this auspicious hour we confer the second cap.
units.literal: The bearer of the Cap of Distant Travels ascended; the crown-placer descended two steps to receive it, holding the nape with his right hand and the front with his left, advanced before the crown prince's seat, stood facing north, and offered the blessing: "On this auspicious hour we add the second cap.

units.zh: 太子興，內侍跪進服，服訖，樂止。
units.en: The crown prince rose while inner attendants knelt to bring forward his garments. Once he was dressed, the music stopped.
units.literal: The crown prince rose; inner attendants knelt to present the garments; when he was dressed, the music ceased.

units.zh: 掌冠者揖太子復坐，掌冠者降 詣罍洗，及讚冠者跪，脫遠遊冠，並如上儀。
units.en: The crown-placer gestured for the crown prince to resume his seat, then went down to the wash basin while the crown-praiser knelt to remove the Cap of Distant Travels, all as before.
units.literal: The crown-placer bowed to the crown prince to return to his seat; the crown-placer descended to the jar and wash-basin, and the crown-praiser knelt and removed the Cap of Distant Travels—all as in the preceding ceremony.

units.zh: 執袞冕者升，掌冠者降三等受之，右執項，左執前，進太子席前，北向立，祝曰：“三加彌尊，國本以正。
units.en: The attendant bearing the imperial robe-and-crown ascended. The crown-placer stepped down three levels to receive it and advanced to stand north-facing before the crown prince's seat. He pronounced the blessing: "With the third investiture ever more exalted, the foundation of the realm is secured.
units.literal: The bearer of the imperial robe-and-cap ascended; the crown-placer descended three steps to receive it, holding the nape with his right hand and the front with his left, advanced before the crown prince's seat, stood facing north, and offered the blessing: "With the third addition ever more honored, the foundation of the state is made right.

units.zh: 太子搢圭，跪受爵，《正安之樂》作，飲訖，奠爵執圭。
units.en: The crown prince inserted his tablet and knelt to receive the goblet as Zheng'an was played. When he had drunk, he set down the goblet and took up his tablet.
units.literal: The crown prince inserted his tablet, knelt to receive the goblet; "Zheng'an" music was performed; when he had drunk, he set down the goblet and held the tablet.

units.zh: 太官令設饌席前，太子搢圭，食訖，樂 止，執圭興，太官令徹饌、爵。
units.en: The Director of the Imperial Kitchen set food before the seat. The crown prince inserted his tablet and ate; when he had finished, the music stopped. He rose holding his tablet, and the Director removed the food and goblet.
units.literal: The Director of the Imperial Kitchen set food before the seat; the crown prince inserted his tablet, ate, and finished; the music ceased; he held the tablet and rose; the Director of the Imperial Kitchen removed the food and goblet.

units.zh: 〈（太子初行，樂作，至位，樂止。）〉
units.en: (When the crown prince first set out, music played; when he reached his station, it stopped.)
units.literal: (When the crown prince first set out, music was performed; when he reached his position, the music ceased.)

units.zh: 左輔承旨，降自東階，詣太子前，西向，宣曰“有敕”，太子再拜，宣敕曰：“事親以孝，接下以仁。
units.en: The Left Assistant received the command, descended the eastern steps, and stood west-facing before the crown prince to announce, "There is an edict." The crown prince double-bowed, and the edict was read: "Serve your parents with filial piety; treat your subordinates with benevolence.
units.literal: The Left Assistant received the command, descended the eastern steps, went before the crown prince, faced west, and announced, "There is an edict"; the crown prince double-bowed; the edict was proclaimed: "Serve your parents with filial piety; treat your subordinates with benevolence.

units.zh: 去為陰沮用兵，進幸蜀之計，宰相陳康伯力非之，帝悟而止。
units.en: Quwei secretly opposed war and urged flight to Shu; Chancellor Chen Kangbo fiercely objected; the emperor saw reason and halted the plan.
units.literal: Quwei secretly discouraged using troops and advanced a plan to move the court to Shu; Chancellor Chen Kangbo strongly opposed it; the Emperor understood and stopped.
